subject: Agriculture
title: Farmer Field Schools
description: A short lesson to help you apply Farmer Field Schools.

hook.text: In the 1980s, Indonesian rice farmers were overusing pesticides and making pest problems worse. Education fixed it.

buildup.text: Farmer Field Schools teach groups of 25 farmers to observe their own fields—counting pests and their predators.

discovery.text: Farmers learned that spraying killed natural enemies, causing pest resurgence. Doing less produced more.

twist.text: FFS-trained farmers reduced pesticide use by 60% while maintaining or increasing yields and profits.

climax.text: Over 10 million farmers across Asia and Africa have graduated from Farmer Field Schools.

punchline.text: The best pest control tool is a trained human eye.

quiz.question: What key insight did Farmer Field School participants gain?
options: Spraying killed natural enemies and caused pest resurgence

details.summary: Farmer field schools are group-based learning programs where farmers conduct hands-on experiments in their own fields to discover effective pest management practices. Developed by the FAO in the 1980s for rice IPM in Asia, the model has spread to over 90 countries.
details.whyItMatters: Farmer field schools have trained millions of farmers in IPM and reduced pesticide use by 35-92% in participating communities. The model empowers farmers as researchers rather than passive recipients of top-down agricultural advice.
takeaways: Farmer field schools use hands-on experimentation rather than classroom instruction
The model originated in Indonesia in 1989 for rice IPM and has reached 90+ countries
Participants typically reduce pesticide use by 35-92% while maintaining or increasing yields

faq.question: How do farmer field schools teach integrated pest management?
faq.answer: Groups of 20-25 farmers meet weekly in a field to observe their crops, identify pests and beneficial insects, and compare plots managed with different strategies. Through season-long experimentation, they discover firsthand which practices work best, building confidence to reduce pesticide use.

faq.question: Have farmer field schools been proven effective at scale?
faq.answer: Studies across Asia, Africa, and Latin America show participants reduce pesticide use significantly while maintaining yields. The FAO estimates over 20 million farmers have graduated from field schools.
